summary: Port Royal is a fast push-your-luck card game where players flip cards from a shared deck into the harbor, deciding when to stop before a duplicate ship type busts their turn, then recruit sellable people or ships for coins and points. It's a snappy filler with real tension in deciding how far to push your luck each turn.
praised: Very quick to teach and play
criticised: Can feel swingy/luck-driven for a 'strategy' game
Limited strategic depth over repeated plays
End-game can drag as scores climb

interaction.detail: Any player can grab cards revealed into the shared harbor before the active player, so there's constant opportunistic sniping of good cards, though each player's own tableau of recruited cards/coins is private. The shared deck and harbor row are the main point of contact between players.

subsystems: hiring persons for VP with type-set bonuses
completing expeditions for VP and rewards
scoring.how_you_win: Push your luck drawing cards to earn coins for hiring persons (worth VP, with bonuses for owning multiple types) and completing expeditions with your ships; once any player reaches 12 points the current round finishes and the highest score wins.
